# Overview

## The Problem

- Reimplementation of @lukeEvolvingTeamworkCoordination1996
- Four lions chasing a gazelle on a toroidal 15×15 grid
- Lions evolve vector-operation trees to coordinate
- Key constraint: **no communication between lions**

## Goal

> Study the emergence of coordination *without communication*

- Coordination must be implicit in evolved behavior
- Three sensing modes × three breeding strategies
- 51 generations, 500 prides per run

---

# Design

## World & Animals

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**World**

- Toroidal 15×15 grid, floating point
- Discrete updates
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Gazelle**

- Moves **3 units/turn** via fear vector:

$$
-\sum_{v \in V} \frac{v}{\|v\|} (\|\text{max}\| - \|v\|)
$$

**Lions**

- Move **1 unit/turn** per evolved tree
- Catch condition: within 1 unit of gazelle
:::
::::

## Operators

| Name | Args | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gazelle` | 0 | Vector lion → gazelle |
| `last` | 0 | Repeat last direction |
| `rand-dir` | 0 | Random unit vector |
| `+` / `-` | 2 / 1 | Add / negate |
| `×2` / `/2` | 1 | Scale magnitude |
| `→90` | 1 | Rotate 90° clockwise |
| `ifdot` / `if>=` | 4 | Conditional branches |

## Sensing Terminals

| Group | Terminals | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Base | *(none)* | No lion-awareness |
| Deictic | `nearest`, `lion`, `rlion`, `llion` | Relative neighbors |
| Name | `lion-0..3` | Named lion vectors |

## Breeding Strategies

- **Clone** — all four lions share one identical tree
- **Free** — any lion breeds with any other
- **Restricted** — lion $i$ only breeds with lion $i$

## Genetic Programming Setup

- Population: 500 prides
- Max depth: 17 / Max size: 70
- Crossover: 90% | Reproduction: 10%
- Selection: tournament ($N=7$)
- Fitness: avg distance − 1 over 5 sims (0 if caught)

## Loss Curves — Name Terminals

```{python}
result_path = Path("results")
path_end = "loss_results.npz"
terminal = "Name"
clone_data = np.load(result_path / experiment / terminal / "Clone" / path_end)
free_data = np.load(result_path / experiment / terminal / "Free" / path_end)
restricted_data = np.load(result_path / experiment / terminal / "Restricted" / path_end)
plot_loss_curves(clone_data, free_data, restricted_data, title=f"{experiment}: {terminal}")
```
